ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

## plugin:context7:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, porting code between libraries, platforms, or SQL dialects, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, debugging, or reviewing code that does not depend on a library or platform API, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:Notion:notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## rea
REA provides reverse-engineering tools for local artifacts, native binaries, managed code, browser pages, and runtimes. Use the tool that directly answers the question; discover targets or inspect inventory only when needed. Tool results include inline Evidence and report their coverage and limitations.

While bypass permissions mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

content.text:
### Spec Compliance
- ✅ README has every §13 section: 실행 절차 (§2), 모듈 구조 + 직접 참조 금지 근거 (§4), CQRS 의도 (§5), 장애 처리 + 시간 예산 (§6), 모니터링/알림 (§7, 3 PromQL), 해석 목록 (§8, 25 items), AI 활용/로깅 preserved.
- ✅ README facts match code and config:
  - Timeouts and ports: connect 500ms, read 1s, ports 8080/8081/9080/9081/15432/15433, loopback bindings (`application.yml`, `compose.yaml`).
  - Retry and limits: `maxRetries=1`, `delay=100ms`, `timeout=1500ms`, concurrency limit 50 (`GroupClientProperties.kt`).
  - Breaker: window 20, min 10 calls, 50% failure rate, open 10s, half-open 3 (`GroupClientProperties.kt`).
  - `Retry-After` is taken from `waitDurationInOpenState` (`MemberExceptionHandler.kt:36`).
  - `management.tracing.export.enabled` is absent from the config, as ruled.
  - Metric names match the Micrometer names in `GroupServiceGateway.kt` (`group.call.duration`, `group.call.failures`, `group.call.permits.in_use`). The http and resilience4j series names come from the implementer's report, which says they were scraped from a running service.
  - Time budget: a retry starts only if elapsed + 100ms < 1.5s, so the worst case is under 2.9s ("약 3초 미만" holds). The test table's 1.0 + 0.1 + 1.0 = 2.1s is consistent.
  - Alerts: URI patterns `/api/member.*` and `/api/group.*` fit the actual routes, and the 0.8s threshold fits the 1s read timeout.
- ✅ Process jargon: grep of README for ledger, brief, "Task N", SDD and fallback found nothing. `scripts/check-forbidden.sh` returned exit 0.
- ✅ The README lists the controller-ruling items: collation, no slow-connect test (§9), tracing export absent, OpenAPI on controllers only.
- ✅ `smoke.sh`:
  - `set -euo pipefail`, jq and curl checks, and the four curl checks are all present.
  - Readiness polling is 90 iterations of 1s per port, with an early exit if Gradle dies.
  - The port pre-check runs before anything starts.
  - `docker compose down -v` runs only when the script started the DBs.
- ✅ OpenAPI: `libs.springdoc.webmvc.ui` is added to both services, annotations are on the controllers only, and `openApiDocIsServed()` exists in both `MemberApiTest` and `GroupApiTest`.
- ✅ Collation: V1 has `collate "ko-x-icu"`. The test compares against the ICU Korean collator. The report says it failed before the migration change (RED at `MemberPagingTest.kt:90`) and passed after. The ASC and DESC test plus the seed triple 강하늘 < 김민수 < 나은 make it genuine, but only the report's RED run proves it, since modern Hangul code-point order is itself dictionary order.
- ⚠️ Cannot verify from the diff: that killing the Gradle client reliably stops both bootRun JVMs, and the smoke and build results.

### Strengths
- The README is thorough and accurate. The reasoning behind the retry-budget classification, the ignoreExceptions rejection, and readiness covering only the member DB is documented.
- The 25-item judgment list matches the ledger.
- The smoke script is compact, and its `check()` helper checks status and body together.

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
None.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
- `scripts/smoke.sh:665-676`: cleanup kills only the Gradle client PID (SIGTERM) and then waits for port 8080 to free. It never confirms the JVMs are gone and has no fallback kill, so a lingering bootRun child would leak. The README says the trap "확인한다" the JVMs went down, but it checks only 8080 and does not fail or force-kill if the port stays bound. Consider starting Gradle in its own process group (`set -m`) and killing that group, or soften the README wording.
- `scripts/smoke.sh:679`: `[ -z "$(docker compose ps -q)" ] && STARTED_DB=1` is false if only one DB container was already running. The script then starts the other one but never tears it down. Rare.
- `scripts/smoke.sh:695-696`: the two readiness waits run one after the other, so the worst case is up to 180s, not the 90s the brief and README imply. The curl calls also have no `-m` timeout.

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Approved
**Reasoning:** The README covers every required section and its numbers, metric names and PromQL match the code and config. The smoke script meets the brief; the cleanup fragility is minor. OpenAPI tests are in both services and the collation fix has a genuine RED-to-GREEN test.
